The idea of task extraction is great in theory. I was hoping Parakeet AI would break down interview questions and give me clear, actionable tasks. results.title: Parakeet AI Review 2026: Is It Worth It and Is It Safe?
results.content:
That last point is the one most people miss. If the tool hands you a solution more sophisticated than you can explain, the interviewer asks a follow-up question and you are stuck. Nobody needed proctoring software to catch that. It is also the one risk no stealth feature can do anything about, which is why we keep saying the useful version of this tool is the practice mode.

Finally, the harshest recent complaint, from August, reports the tool doing nothing at all:

> "I have purchased credits for interview for parakeet ai. It's literally just shows transcript of interaction. Nothing else. It does not provide answers not as easy as shown in advertisement. Literally waste of money."sabarinath jaladanki, Trustpilot, August 2026 [...] The problem is that interviews are not casual calls, and this is exactly where the cracks show. Users report it freezing, overwriting good answers, and looping on coding problems at the worst possible moment. Support and refunds draw steady complaints. And the headline promise, that you are invisible, is the part that fails hardest, both in software and in front of a human. Add the fact that a growing number of employers will disqualify you for using it, and the math gets hard to justify. [...] > "I've used Parakeet AI a few times and found it quite inconsistent. Occasionally it gives the right answers, but most of the time it struggles to properly understand the questions, which makes it unreliable for real interview use... I don't think it's ready to be a paid product yet."Tarik, Trustpilot, April 2026

Another, from a reviewer named Kridge, is the billing complaint that came up again and again:

 A one star Trustpilot review titled Unreliable and still charging, describing frozen answers and a refused refund
